claim.pdf_says: Page 1025 (printed 995) ends with "Saurashtra:\nA880-A881, A8B4-A8C5, A8D0-A8D9". "Sharada:" is the FIRST line printed on page 1026 (printed 996), directly above "11180-11182, 111B3-111C0, 111C9-111CC, 111CE-111D9".
claim.markdown_says: End of the page-1025 block: "A880-A881, A8B4-A8C5, A8D0-A8D9 Sharada:". The page-1026 block then opens with a headless "11180-11182, 111B3-111C0, 111C9-111CC, 111CE-111D9".
claim.why_it_matters: Sharada's code-point ranges are left unattributed in the normative Annex B table and the Saurashtra entry carries a stray label.

verdict.reasoning: Both quotations are literally accurate, but the difference is page-break furniture, which the verification rules exclude. Rendered PDF p1025 (printed 995) does end at 'Saurashtra: / A880-A881, A8B4-A8C5, A8D0-A8D9' with no Sharada line, and rendered p1026 (printed 996) does open with 'Sharada: / 11180-11182, 111B3-111C0, 111C9-111CC, 111CE-111D9'. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 40981 reads 'A880-A881, A8B4-A8C5, A8D0-A8D9 Sharada:' and the page-1026 block (lines 40983-40987) opens with the bare range list. THREE findings defeat the claim. (1) NO CONTENT IS LOST OR ALTERED: the token 'Sharada:' is present, every script name and every code-point range on p1025 is byte-identical to the PDF (verified entry by entry, Mongolian through Saurashtra), and no range is changed, added, or dropped. (2) ATTRIBUTION IS NOT BROKEN: the only text separating 'Sharada:' from '11180-11182, ...' is the transcription's own injected page-break furniture (the '' anchor, the '## Page 1026' heading, and the running header '# ISO\IEC 1989:2023 (E)'). Strip that synthetic furniture, as any reader of the running text does, and the sequence reads '...A8D0-A8D9 Sharada: 11180-11182, ...' -- the label still immediately precedes its own ranges. The ranges are not 'left unattributed'; they are attributed across an artificial marker. (3) IT IS A UNIFORM PIPELINE ARTIFACT, NOT A p1025 DEFECT: grepping for the pattern 'hex-range line ending in a trailing Label:' returns ~19 hits, one at essentially every page seam of this Annex script/code-point listing -- lines 40182 (Ahom), 40235 (Buhid), 40403 (Kaithi), 40454 (Linear_B), 40506 (Miao), 40558 (Old_Italic), 40610 (Rejang), 40772 (Buhid), 40824 (Gunjala_Gondi), 40876 (Khojki), 40928 (Mongolian), 40981 (Sharada), 49030 (Brahmi), 49087 (Deseret), 49207 (Kannada), 49263 (Lydian), 49319 (Multani), 49374 (Old_Turkic), 49431 (Sinhala). The very same artifact supplies p1025's own missing top label: 'Mongolian:' sits at the end of the p1024 block on line 40928, which is why the p1025 block also opens headless with '180B-180D, 1810-1819, 18A9'. The transcriber consistently places the next page's first label on the last text line before the page marker. This is a boundary line-placement behavior of the extraction, i.e. formatting, not a content discrepancy. Meaning is unchanged: the same 16 scripts with the same ranges appear on p1025 in the same order, and Sharada keeps the same ranges. Per the rejection criteria ('page-break furniture ... or formatting' and 'the difference does not change meaning'), this is not a real finding.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The transcription systematically appends the FIRST script label of the next PDF page to the LAST text line of the current page's block, immediately before the injected page anchor / '## Page N' heading / running header. 'Sharada:' at the tail of line 40981 is one of ~19 identical page-seam occurrences in this Annex listing (the reciprocal case, 'Mongolian:' parked on line 40928, is why the p1025 block itself starts headless). No script name, no code-point range, and no attribution is lost -- with the synthetic page furniture removed the label still directly precedes its own ranges. If it is worth logging at all, it is a single document-wide COSMETIC/formatting note against the transcription pipeline's page-boundary line splitting, not a structural per-page defect at p1025, and it warrants no edit to the normative content.
